name: Roman Empire
modern_places: Italy; France; Spain; Portugal; Greece; Turkey; Egypt; England; Britain; Tunisia; Syria; Israel; Balkans; Mediterranean
territory: The Mediterranean basin: Western and Southern Europe, North Africa and the Near East
language_faith: Latin, with Greek in the east; traditional polytheism, then Christianity as state religion from 380
fact: Reached its greatest extent around 117 CE, roughly 5 million km², ringed by fortified frontiers.

name: Byzantine Empire
aliases: byzantium; eastern roman; eastern roman empire; byzantine
modern_places: Turkey; Greece; Bulgaria; Italy; Egypt; Syria; Balkans; Istanbul
territory: Southeastern Europe, Anatolia and the eastern Mediterranean
language_faith: Greek; Orthodox Christianity
fact: Completed the domed Hagia Sophia in 537 and preserved classical Greek texts for a thousand years.

name: Ottoman Empire
modern_places: Turkey; Greece; Bulgaria; Serbia; Hungary; Egypt; Iraq; Syria; Saudi Arabia; Algeria; Libya; Balkans; Middle East; Istanbul
territory: Anatolia, the Balkans, the Middle East and North Africa
language_faith: Ottoman Turkish; Sunni Islam
fact: Besieged Vienna in 1529 and again in 1683, and claimed the caliphate from 1517.

name: Mongol Empire
modern_places: Mongolia; China; Russia; Iran; Persia; Korea; Kazakhstan; Ukraine; Central Asia
territory: From Korea and China across Central Asia to Eastern Europe
language_faith: Mongolian; Tengrism, with wide religious tolerance
fact: The largest contiguous land empire in history, about 24 million km² at its peak.

name: Achaemenid Empire
modern_places: Iran; Persia; Iraq; Turkey; Egypt; Afghanistan; Pakistan; Syria; Israel; Central Asia
territory: The Iranian plateau, stretching from Egypt and Anatolia to the Indus
language_faith: Old Persian, Elamite and Aramaic; Zoroastrianism
fact: Built a 2,700 km Royal Road with relay stations, and let exiles held in Babylon return home.

name: Han dynasty
territory: China, reaching into Korea, Vietnam and the Tarim Basin
language_faith: Old Chinese; Confucianism as state ideology, plus Taoism
fact: Opened Silk Road trade with the west and produced the first known paper. China's largest ethnic group still carries its name.

name: Qin dynasty
territory: Northern and central China
language_faith: Old Chinese; Legalism
fact: First to unify China. Standardized script, coins, weights and even cart axle widths; buried thousands of clay soldiers.

name: Tang dynasty
territory: China and Central Asia along the Silk Road
language_faith: Middle Chinese; Buddhism, Taoism and Confucianism
fact: A golden age of Chinese poetry and early woodblock printing; its capital held around a million people.

name: Ming dynasty
territory: China
language_faith: Mandarin Chinese; Neo-Confucianism
fact: Sent huge treasure fleets as far as East Africa, built the Forbidden City and rebuilt the Great Wall in brick.

name: Qing dynasty
territory: China, Mongolia, Tibet and Xinjiang
language_faith: Manchu, Chinese and Mongolian; Confucianism and Tibetan Buddhism
fact: Founded by a people from the northeast beyond the Great Wall; China's last imperial dynasty, weakened by the Opium Wars.

name: Maurya Empire
territory: Nearly the whole Indian subcontinent and parts of Afghanistan
language_faith: Prakrit; Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism
fact: Its rock and pillar edicts preached non-violence; one pillar's lion capital is now India's national emblem.

name: Gupta Empire
territory: Northern and central India
language_faith: Sanskrit; Hinduism
fact: India's classical golden age: Aryabhata's astronomy, Kalidasa's plays and the place-value decimal system.

name: Mughal Empire
territory: Most of the Indian subcontinent
language_faith: Persian at court, later Urdu; Islam, with notable tolerance under one emperor
fact: Built the Taj Mahal and the Red Fort; around 1700 it produced nearly a quarter of world output.
capital: Agra, Fatehpur Sikri, Lahore and Delhi

name: Aztec Empire
territory: Central Mexico
language_faith: Nahuatl; Mexica religion centered on the sun and war god Huitzilopochtli
fact: Its island capital in a lake was fed by floating farm plots and held perhaps 200,000 people.

name: Inca Empire
modern_places: Peru; Ecuador; Bolivia; Chile; Argentina; Colombia
territory: The Andes of western South America
language_faith: Quechua; worship of the sun god Inti
fact: Ran a 40,000 km road network and kept records on knotted cords, without wheels or a written script.

name: Mali Empire
modern_places: Mali; Senegal; Guinea; Gambia; Mauritania; West Africa
territory: West Africa's Sahel, along the upper Niger River
language_faith: Manding languages; Islam blended with traditional beliefs
fact: Its ruler's 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca carried so much gold that prices in Cairo slumped for years.

name: Songhai Empire
territory: West Africa along the middle Niger River
language_faith: Songhay; Islam
fact: The largest state in West African history, broken by a Moroccan army with firearms at Tondibi.

name: Ghana Empire
territory: West African Sahel, in today's Mauritania and Mali
language_faith: Soninke; traditional religion, later Islam
fact: Grew rich taxing the trans-Saharan trade of gold for salt; an Andalusian geographer described its court in 1068.
ruler: Kings of the Soninke Cissé dynasty

name: Kingdom of Aksum
aliases: aksum; axum; aksumite empire; axumite empire
territory: The Horn of Africa, across the Red Sea into southern Arabia
language_faith: Ge'ez; Christianity from the 4th century
fact: Among the first states to adopt Christianity and to mint its own coins; known for giant carved granite stelae.

name: Carthage
modern_places: Tunisia; Libya; Algeria; Spain; Italy; Sicily
territory: North Africa (Tunisia), Sicily, Sardinia and southern Iberia
language_faith: Punic; Phoenician gods Baal Hammon and Tanit
fact: Its general crossed the Alps with war elephants in 218 BCE; its enemy later razed the city.

name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
aliases: assyria; assyrian; assyrian empire; neo assyrian
modern_places: Iraq; Syria; Turkey; Israel; Egypt; Iran; Mesopotamia
territory: Northern Mesopotamia, extending to the Levant and Egypt
language_faith: Akkadian and Aramaic; Mesopotamian religion led by the god Ashur
fact: A royal library of over 30,000 clay tablets preserved the Epic of Gilgamesh.

name: Akkadian Empire
territory: Mesopotamia (modern Iraq) and parts of Syria and Iran
language_faith: Akkadian and Sumerian; Mesopotamian gods
fact: Often called the first empire. The founder's daughter Enheduanna is the earliest author known by name.
capital: Akkad (its site has never been found)

name: Neo-Babylonian Empire
aliases: babylon; babylonian; babylonian empire; chaldean empire; neo babylonian
territory: Mesopotamia and the Levant
language_faith: Akkadian and Aramaic; worship of Marduk
fact: Raised the blue-glazed Ishtar Gate and destroyed Jerusalem's First Temple in 587 BCE.

name: New Kingdom of Egypt
aliases: egypt; egyptian empire; new kingdom; egyptian new kingdom; ancient egypt
territory: The Nile valley, Nubia and the Levant
language_faith: Egyptian; polytheism led by Amun-Ra
fact: One ruler briefly forced worship of a single sun disk; later kings were buried in a hidden valley of rock tombs.

name: Hittite Empire
territory: Anatolia and northern Syria
language_faith: Hittite, the oldest written Indo-European language; the 'thousand gods'
fact: Fought Egypt at Kadesh in 1274 BCE, then signed one of the earliest known peace treaties.

name: Umayyad Caliphate
modern_places: Syria; Spain; Portugal; Iraq; Iran; Egypt; Saudi Arabia; Morocco; Pakistan; Middle East
territory: From Iberia across North Africa and the Middle East to the Indus
language_faith: Arabic; Islam
fact: Built the Dome of the Rock and made Arabic the language of government across its lands.

name: Abbasid Caliphate
modern_places: Iraq; Iran; Syria; Egypt; Saudi Arabia; Middle East
territory: The Middle East, North Africa and Persia
language_faith: Arabic and Persian; Islam
fact: Its House of Wisdom anchored the Islamic Golden Age; it ended when the Mongols sacked its capital.

name: Holy Roman Empire
modern_places: Germany; Austria; Czechia; Italy; Netherlands; Belgium; Switzerland
territory: Central Europe: the German lands, Bohemia, Austria and northern Italy
language_faith: German, Latin, Italian and Czech; Catholicism, later also Protestantism
fact: Its emperors were chosen by prince-electors; Voltaire joked it was neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire.
capital: No fixed capital; Aachen, Prague and Vienna at different times

name: Carolingian Empire
modern_places: France; Germany; Italy; Netherlands; Belgium; Switzerland
territory: Western and Central Europe
language_faith: Latin and Frankish; Catholicism
fact: Its founder was crowned by the Pope on Christmas Day; his grandsons split it at Verdun in 843.

name: Khmer Empire
territory: Mainland Southeast Asia: Cambodia, Thailand, Laos and southern Vietnam
language_faith: Old Khmer and Sanskrit; Hinduism, then Buddhism
fact: Built the largest religious monument on Earth and vast reservoirs to water its rice fields.

name: Srivijaya
territory: Maritime Southeast Asia: Sumatra, Java and the Malay Peninsula
language_faith: Old Malay and Sanskrit; Mahayana Buddhism
fact: Controlled shipping through the Strait of Malacca; a Chinese monk stopped there in 671 to study Buddhism.

name: Majapahit
territory: Java and much of the Indonesian archipelago
language_faith: Old Javanese; Hindu-Buddhist
fact: Its chief minister swore not to enjoy spices until the archipelago was united under one crown.

name: Russian Empire
modern_places: Russia; Ukraine; Finland; Poland; Kazakhstan; Georgia; Alaska; Central Asia
territory: Eastern Europe and Northern Asia, with Alaska until 1867
language_faith: Russian; Eastern Orthodoxy
fact: Spanned three continents; its rulers abolished serfdom in 1861 and fell during World War I.

name: British Empire
modern_places: United Kingdom; Britain; England; India; Pakistan; Canada; Australia; New Zealand; South Africa; Egypt; Nigeria; Kenya; America; Ireland; Hong Kong
territory: Global, with holdings on every inhabited continent
language_faith: English; Anglicanism, among many faiths
fact: By the 1920s it governed about a quarter of the world's land and people, so the sun never set on it.

name: Spanish Empire
modern_places: Spain; Mexico; Peru; Philippines; Argentina; Colombia; Cuba; Chile; America
territory: The Americas, the Philippines and parts of Europe and Africa
language_faith: Spanish; Catholicism
fact: Silver from a single Andean mountain flooded world trade and helped make the first truly global currency.

name: Portuguese Empire
modern_places: Portugal; Brazil; Angola; Mozambique; India; Macau
territory: Coastal Africa, Brazil, India and East Asian trading posts
language_faith: Portuguese; Catholicism
fact: First to sail around Africa to India (1498), and the last European power to hand back a colony in Asia.

name: Empire of Japan
territory: The Japanese islands, Korea, Taiwan and much of East Asia and the Pacific
language_faith: Japanese; State Shinto
fact: Turned a feudal society into an industrial power within a generation and defeated Russia in 1905.

name: Sasanian Empire
aliases: sasanian; sassanid; sassanian; sasanid; sassanid empire
territory: Iran, Mesopotamia and the Caucasus
language_faith: Middle Persian; Zoroastrianism
fact: Captured a Roman emperor in battle in 260, and fell to the early Arab conquests.

name: Parthian Empire
territory: Iran and Mesopotamia
language_faith: Parthian and Greek; Zoroastrianism
fact: Its horse archers shot backward while retreating, and they destroyed Crassus's legions at Carrhae in 53 BCE.

name: Seleucid Empire
territory: Syria, Mesopotamia and Iran
language_faith: Greek and Aramaic; Greek and local gods
fact: Formed from the largest share of Alexander's conquests; it got 500 war elephants in a treaty with an Indian king.
capital: Seleucia on the Tigris, then Antioch

name: Timurid Empire
modern_places: Uzbekistan; Iran; Persia; Afghanistan; Central Asia
territory: Central Asia, Iran and Afghanistan
language_faith: Persian and Chagatai Turkic; Sunni Islam
fact: The founder's grandson built one of the finest observatories of the medieval world.

name: Safavid Empire
territory: Iran, the Caucasus and parts of Iraq and Afghanistan
language_faith: Persian and Azerbaijani Turkic; Twelver Shia Islam
fact: Made Shia Islam Iran's state religion; its capital was praised as 'half the world'.

name: Ethiopian Empire
territory: The Ethiopian highlands of the Horn of Africa
language_faith: Ge'ez and Amharic; Ethiopian Orthodox Christianity
fact: Crushed an invading Italian army at Adwa in 1896, one of the few African states never colonized.

name: Kushan Empire
modern_places: India; Pakistan; Afghanistan; Uzbekistan; Tajikistan; Central Asia
territory: Central Asia, Afghanistan, Pakistan and northern India
language_faith: Bactrian and Gandhari; Buddhism, Zoroastrianism and Hinduism
fact: Gandharan art fused Greek and Buddhist styles, and Buddhism traveled from here into China.

name: Chola Empire
territory: South India, Sri Lanka and coastal Southeast Asia
language_faith: Tamil; Hinduism (Shaivism)
fact: Launched an overseas naval raid on Srivijaya in 1025 and built the towering temple at Thanjavur.

name: Vijayanagara Empire
territory: South India's Deccan plateau
language_faith: Kannada and Telugu; Hinduism
fact: Portuguese visitors compared its capital to Rome; its army was shattered at Talikota in 1565.

name: Austria-Hungary
aliases: austro hungarian empire; austro hungary; austria hungary; dual monarchy; austrian empire
modern_places: Austria; Hungary; Czechia; Slovakia; Croatia; Bosnia; Slovenia; Poland; Ukraine; Romania
territory: Central and Eastern Europe
language_faith: German, Hungarian, Czech and a dozen more; mostly Catholicism
fact: A dual monarchy with two parliaments; its heir's assassination in Sarajevo set off World War I.

name: First French Empire
aliases: french empire; napoleonic empire; french; first empire
territory: Western and Central Europe
language_faith: French; Catholicism
fact: Issued a civil code still at the root of many legal systems; dominated the continent until defeat in Belgium.

name: German Empire
aliases: second reich; imperial germany; germany; kaiserreich
territory: Central Europe, plus colonies in Africa and the Pacific
language_faith: German; Protestantism and Catholicism
fact: Proclaimed in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles; pioneered state pensions and health insurance.

name: Seljuk Empire
aliases: seljuk; seljuks; great seljuk empire; seljuq; great seljuq
modern_places: Iran; Persia; Turkey; Iraq; Turkmenistan; Central Asia
territory: Iran, Mesopotamia, Central Asia and Anatolia
language_faith: Persian and Oghuz Turkic; Sunni Islam
fact: Its victory at Manzikert in 1071 opened Anatolia to Turkic settlement and helped trigger the First Crusade.

name: Golden Horde
territory: The Pontic–Caspian steppe, from Ukraine to Kazakhstan
language_faith: Kipchak Turkic and Mongolian; Tengrism, then Islam
fact: Collected tribute from the Rus' principalities for more than two centuries.

name: Yuan dynasty
territory: China and Mongolia, with Korea as a vassal
language_faith: Mongolian and Chinese; Tibetan Buddhism with broad tolerance
fact: The first foreign dynasty to rule all of China, it issued paper money; Marco Polo claimed to serve its court.

name: Delhi Sultanate
territory: Northern India
language_faith: Persian; Islam
fact: Turned back repeated Mongol invasions and raised the 73-metre Qutb Minar.

name: Kingdom of Nepal
aliases: nepal; gorkha; gorkha kingdom; kingdom of gorkha; shah dynasty
territory: The central Himalaya; at its peak it stretched from the Teesta River in the east to the Sutlej in the west
language_faith: Nepali; Hinduism
fact: Born from a hill state's conquest of the Kathmandu Valley; lost about a third of its land to the East India Company under the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli, and became a republic by parliamentary vote.

name: Licchavi Kingdom
territory: The Kathmandu Valley and the surrounding hills
language_faith: Sanskrit; Hinduism and Buddhism
fact: Left Nepal's oldest dated inscription, carved on a pillar at the Changu Narayan temple in 464.

name: Malla dynasty
aliases: malla; mallas; malla kingdom; malla nepal
territory: The Kathmandu Valley, later split into three rival kingdoms
language_faith: Newar (Nepal Bhasa) and Sanskrit; Hinduism and Buddhism
fact: Split into three rival city-kingdoms whose palace squares are now World Heritage sites; the last fell in a single campaign of conquest.
capital: Bhaktapur, later also Kathmandu and Patan

name: Maratha Empire
territory: Much of the Indian subcontinent, from the Deccan plateau to Punjab at its height
language_faith: Marathi; Hinduism
fact: Its armies reached Attock and Peshawar in 1758, then suffered a crushing defeat at Panipat in 1761.

name: Sikh Empire
aliases: sikh; khalsa raj; sarkar-i-khalsa; punjab empire
territory: Punjab, Kashmir and the Khyber frontier
language_faith: Punjabi, with Persian at court; Sikhism, ruling Hindu and Muslim subjects
fact: Its ruler owned the Koh-i-Noor diamond; annexed by the British after two hard-fought wars.

name: Pala Empire
territory: Bengal and Bihar, at times much of northern India
language_faith: Sanskrit and early Bengali; Mahayana Buddhism
fact: Patron of the monastic universities of Nalanda and Vikramashila, which drew students from Tibet and Southeast Asia.

name: Tibetan Empire
modern_places: China; Tibet; Nepal; Bhutan; India; Central Asia; Himalaya
territory: The Tibetan plateau, reaching into Central Asia, western China and the Himalaya
language_faith: Old Tibetan; Bon, then Buddhism
fact: Briefly captured the Tang capital Chang'an in 763, and adapted an Indian script to write its language.

name: Song dynasty
territory: China proper; after 1127 only the south, below the Huai River
language_faith: Middle Chinese; Neo-Confucianism, Buddhism and Taoism
fact: The first government to issue paper money and the first to use gunpowder weapons in war; finally conquered by the Mongols.

name: Goguryeo
territory: Northern Korea and Manchuria
language_faith: Goguryeo (Old Korean); Buddhism and shamanism
fact: Repelled massive Chinese invasions by the Sui dynasty in 612; the name 'Korea' ultimately traces back to it.

name: Silla
aliases: shilla; unified silla; kingdom of silla
territory: Southeastern Korea, then most of the peninsula after 676
language_faith: Old Korean; Buddhism
fact: Allied with Tang China to unify most of Korea; its capital's Cheomseongdae is one of East Asia's oldest surviving observatories.

name: Goryeo
territory: The Korean peninsula
language_faith: Middle Korean; Buddhism
fact: Printed the Jikji (1377), the oldest surviving book printed with metal movable type; the English name 'Korea' comes from it.

name: Joseon
aliases: chosun; choson; joseon dynasty; yi dynasty
territory: The Korean peninsula
language_faith: Korean, with Classical Chinese at court; Neo-Confucianism
fact: Its fourth king created the Hangul alphabet; it ended as the short-lived Korean Empire.

name: Tokugawa shogunate
aliases: tokugawa; edo shogunate; edo bakufu; tokugawa bakufu
territory: The Japanese islands
language_faith: Japanese; Buddhism, Shinto and Neo-Confucianism
fact: Closed Japan to most foreign contact for over two centuries, admitting Dutch traders only to a small island in Nagasaki harbor.

name: Pagan Kingdom
aliases: pagan; bagan; pagan empire; bagan kingdom
territory: The Irrawaddy valley, uniting most of modern Myanmar
language_faith: Old Burmese and Pali; Theravada Buddhism
fact: Raised over 10,000 temples and stupas on one plain; more than 2,000 still stand.

name: Ayutthaya Kingdom
territory: Central Thailand, with sway over much of mainland Southeast Asia
language_faith: Thai; Theravada Buddhism
fact: A cosmopolitan trading port built on an island in the Chao Phraya River; razed by a Burmese army in 1767.

name: Konbaung dynasty
aliases: konbaung; third burmese empire; alaungpaya dynasty
territory: Burma, at times Manipur and Assam
language_faith: Burmese; Theravada Buddhism
fact: Destroyed Ayutthaya in 1767, then lost three wars to the British; its last king was exiled to India.

name: Lý dynasty
aliases: ly; ly dynasty; dai viet; đại việt
territory: Northern Vietnam (the Red River delta)
language_faith: Vietnamese, with Classical Chinese in writing; Buddhism
fact: Moved its capital to Thăng Long (modern Hanoi) in 1010 and founded the Temple of Literature, Vietnam's first university.

name: Kingdom of Kush
territory: The Nile valley south of Egypt, in modern Sudan
language_faith: Meroitic and Egyptian; Egyptian and Nubian gods such as Amun and Apedemak
fact: Its kings ruled Egypt as the 25th Dynasty, and its royal cemeteries hold more pyramids than all of Egypt.

name: Ptolemaic Kingdom
territory: Egypt, with Cyrenaica, Cyprus and parts of the Levant
language_faith: Greek and Egyptian; Greek and Egyptian gods, including the hybrid Serapis
fact: Built the Library and the Lighthouse of Alexandria; its last ruler sided with Mark Antony and lost.

name: Kingdom of Zimbabwe
territory: The plateau between the Zambezi and Limpopo rivers
language_faith: Early Shona; ancestral religion
fact: Raised massive stone walls without mortar; Chinese porcelain found there shows Indian Ocean trade. A modern country took its name.

name: Kingdom of Kongo
territory: The lower Congo River and northern Angola
language_faith: Kikongo, with Portuguese at court; Catholicism blended with traditional belief
fact: Its king became Catholic in 1491; his son later wrote to the king of Portugal protesting the slave trade.

name: Kingdom of Benin
aliases: benin kingdom; edo kingdom; benin empire
territory: The rainforest of what is now southern Nigeria
language_faith: Edo; Edo traditional religion
fact: Famed for brass plaques and heads that a British expedition looted in 1897; many are still held in museums abroad.

name: Oyo Empire
territory: Yorubaland and the savanna to the west, in modern Nigeria and Benin
language_faith: Yoruba; Yoruba religion, including the thunder god Shango
fact: Its cavalry forced the kingdom of Dahomey to pay tribute for most of a century; it broke apart after a revolt in its own provincial capital.

name: Ashanti Empire
aliases: ashanti; asante; asante empire; asante union
modern_places: Ghana; Ivory Coast; Togo; West Africa
territory: Central and southern Ghana
language_faith: Twi; Akan religion
fact: United around a Golden Stool said to have descended from the sky; fought Britain in the War of the Golden Stool in 1900.

name: Zulu Kingdom
territory: Northeastern South Africa, between the Tugela and Pongola rivers
language_faith: Zulu; Zulu traditional religion
fact: Its army destroyed a British force at Isandlwana in 1879, one of the worst defeats of a modern army by an indigenous one.

name: Chimú Kingdom
aliases: chimu; chimor; kingdom of chimor; chimu empire
territory: The northern coast of Peru
language_faith: Quingnam and Mochica; moon worship
fact: Its adobe capital was the largest city of pre-Columbian South America; conquered by a rising highland power.

name: Tiwanaku
territory: The Lake Titicaca basin, with colonies down to the Pacific coast
language_faith: Unknown, possibly Puquina; worship of a staff-holding creator god
fact: Built the Gateway of the Sun at nearly 3,850 m above sea level, one of the highest cities ever built.

name: Empire of Brazil
territory: Brazil, plus Uruguay until 1828
language_faith: Portuguese; Catholicism
fact: The only lasting monarchy in the independent Americas; it abolished slavery in 1888, a year before the emperor was deposed.

name: Macedonian Empire
aliases: macedon; macedonia; alexander's empire; empire of alexander
modern_places: Greece; North Macedonia; Turkey; Egypt; Iran; Persia; Iraq; Afghanistan; Pakistan; Balkans
territory: From Greece and Egypt across the Persian lands to the Indus
language_faith: Ancient Greek; Greek gods
fact: Conquered from Greece to the Indus in about a decade without losing a major battle, founding many cities named after its ruler.

name: Kievan Rus'
aliases: kievan rus; kyivan rus; rus; kiev rus
territory: The forests and rivers from the Baltic to the Black Sea
language_faith: Old East Slavic; Slavic paganism, then Orthodox Christianity
fact: Founded by Scandinavian Varangians; its prince's baptism in 988 brought Orthodox Christianity to the East Slavs. Destroyed by the Mongols.

name: First Bulgarian Empire
modern_places: Bulgaria; Romania; Serbia; North Macedonia; Greece; Balkans
territory: The eastern Balkans and the lower Danube
language_faith: Old Church Slavonic; Tengrism, then Orthodox Christianity
fact: The Cyrillic script took shape at its literary schools; a Byzantine emperor reportedly blinded 15,000 of its captured soldiers.

name: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
aliases: poland; polish lithuanian commonwealth; commonwealth of two nations; rzeczpospolita; poland lithuania
modern_places: Poland; Lithuania; Belarus; Ukraine; Latvia; Russia
territory: One of Europe's largest states, from the Baltic almost to the Black Sea
language_faith: Polish, Latin and Ruthenian; Catholicism, with unusual religious tolerance
fact: Its nobles elected their kings, and a single deputy could veto parliament; partitioned out of existence by three neighbors.

name: Swedish Empire
modern_places: Sweden; Finland; Estonia; Latvia; Germany; Russia; Baltic
territory: The lands around the Baltic Sea
language_faith: Swedish; Lutheranism
fact: Dominated the Baltic for a century; its huge warship Vasa sank on its maiden voyage in 1628.

name: Dutch Empire
aliases: netherlands; dutch; dutch colonial empire; dutch republic
modern_places: Netherlands; Indonesia; Suriname; South Africa; Sri Lanka; Taiwan; Brazil; America; Guyana; Caribbean
map_places: Netherlands; Indonesia; Suriname; South Africa; Sri Lanka; Taiwan; Guyana
territory: Trading posts and colonies from the East Indies to the Caribbean
language_faith: Dutch; Dutch Reformed Christianity
fact: Its East India Company is often called the first publicly traded company; it gave up New Amsterdam, later New York, to England.

name: Rashidun Caliphate
modern_places: Saudi Arabia; Iraq; Iran; Persia; Syria; Egypt; Israel; Middle East
territory: Arabia, then Persia, the Levant and Egypt
language_faith: Arabic; Islam
fact: Conquered the Sasanian Empire and Byzantine Syria and Egypt in about twenty years; three of its four leaders were assassinated.

name: Fatimid Caliphate
modern_places: Egypt; Tunisia; Algeria; Libya; Syria; Israel; Sicily; Saudi Arabia; Middle East
territory: North Africa, Egypt, the Levant and western Arabia
language_faith: Arabic; Ismaili Shia Islam
fact: Founded Cairo in 969 along with the Al-Azhar mosque, now one of the world's oldest working universities.

name: Ayyubid Sultanate
modern_places: Egypt; Syria; Yemen; Iraq; Israel; Saudi Arabia; Middle East
territory: Egypt, Syria, Upper Mesopotamia, Yemen and western Arabia
language_faith: Arabic and Kurdish; Sunni Islam
fact: Its Kurdish founder retook Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187.

name: Mamluk Sultanate
modern_places: Egypt; Syria; Israel; Saudi Arabia; Middle East
territory: Egypt, the Levant and the Hejaz
language_faith: Arabic, with Kipchak Turkic in the army; Sunni Islam
fact: Ruled by former slave-soldiers; stopped the Mongol advance at Ain Jalut in 1260.

name: Ghaznavid Empire
modern_places: Afghanistan; Iran; Persia; Pakistan; India; Central Asia
territory: Afghanistan, eastern Iran and the Punjab
language_faith: Persian; Sunni Islam
fact: Its sultan raided India around 17 times; the poet Ferdowsi finished the Shahnameh in its time.

name: Tuʻi Tonga Empire
aliases: tui tonga; tu'i tonga; tonga; tongan empire
modern_places: Tonga; Samoa; Fiji; Wallis and Futuna; Niue; Polynesia; Pacific
territory: Tonga, with influence across Samoa, Fiji and other islands of western Polynesia
language_faith: Tongan; Polynesian religion, later Christianity
fact: Its sacred kings ruled from Tongatapu, where a later king raised the Haʻamonga ʻa Maui, a massive coral-stone trilithon.

name: Saudeleur dynasty
territory: The island of Pohnpei in Micronesia
language_faith: Pohnpeian; worship of the thunder god Nahnisohn Sahpw
fact: Ruled from nearly 100 artificial islets built of stacked basalt columns on a coral reef; overthrown by an invader from Kosrae.

name: Kingdom of Hawaii
aliases: hawaii; hawaiian kingdom; kingdom of hawai'i
modern_places: Hawaii; United States; America; Polynesia; Pacific
territory: The Hawaiian Islands
language_faith: Hawaiian and English; native religion, then Christianity
fact: Its last monarch was overthrown in 1893 by American businessmen backed by US Marines; annexed by the US in 1898.

name: Kingdom of Tahiti
territory: Tahiti and nearby islands of the Society Islands
language_faith: Tahitian; Christianity, adopted under the second king
fact: Became a French protectorate in 1842 and was annexed by France in 1880.

name: Kingdom of Fiji
territory: The Fiji Islands
language_faith: Fijian and English; Methodist Christianity
fact: Lasted barely three years; amid debts and unrest, its king ceded the islands to Britain.

name: Teotihuacan
territory: The Valley of Mexico, with influence reaching the Maya lowlands
language_faith: Unknown, perhaps an early Nahua or Totonac tongue; a storm god and the Feathered Serpent
fact: Built the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon along a 2 km avenue and was one of the largest cities on Earth, perhaps 100,000 people. The Aztecs found it in ruins and gave it the name we use.
capital: The city itself, in the Valley of Mexico
ruler: Spearthrower Owl, a ruler named in Maya inscriptions

name: Toltec Empire
territory: Central Mexico, around the Tula valley in today's Hidalgo
language_faith: Probably Nahuatl; the cult of the Feathered Serpent
fact: Later peoples remembered them as master craftsmen. Their giant stone warrior columns still stand, and their style turns up at Chichén Itzá, far to the south.

name: Tarascan State
aliases: purépecha empire; purepecha empire; tarascan empire; purépecha; purepecha
territory: Michoacán and the neighbouring lands of western Mexico
language_faith: A language unrelated to any other; worship of the fire god Curicaueri
fact: Crushed an Aztec army in 1478, one of the Aztecs' worst defeats. Unusually for Mesoamerica, its smiths made tools of copper and bronze.

name: Kingdom of Tikal
territory: The central Petén lowlands of northern Guatemala
language_faith: Classic Mayan; divine kings and ancestor worship
fact: Its temples still rise above the rainforest canopy. A long war with Calakmul, the rival 'snake kingdom', shaped two centuries of Maya politics.

name: League of Mayapan
territory: The northern Yucatán peninsula
language_faith: Yucatec Maya; the cult of Kukulkan, the Feathered Serpent
fact: The last great Maya capital, a walled city of about 15,000 people. It fell to a revolt around 1450, and the Spanish later had to fight the rival states it left one by one.

name: Cahokia
territory: The Mississippi floodplain opposite today's St. Louis
language_faith: Unknown, perhaps a Siouan language; a sky-and-sun religion built around platform mounds
fact: Its great earthen mound is the largest prehistoric earthwork in the Americas. Around 1100 the town may have been as big as London was then.
capital: The mound city itself, on the Mississippi
ruler: No rulers' names survive; its copper plates show a falcon-dancer, the 'Birdman'

name: Powhatan Confederacy
territory: Tidewater Virginia, along the rivers feeding Chesapeake Bay
language_faith: An Algonquian language; worship of Okeus and Ahone
fact: Its paramount chief met the first lasting English settlers in 1607. His daughter married one of them and died in England.

name: Comanchería
territory: The southern Great Plains: west Texas, eastern New Mexico, western Oklahoma and southern Kansas
language_faith: A Numic (Uto-Aztecan) language; vision quests and the Great Spirit
fact: Masters of the horse, its riders raided deep into Mexico and held back Spanish expansion for a century. It fell only after the bison herds were slaughtered.
capital: None; its bands moved with the herds

name: New France
aliases: nouvelle-france; french canada; french north america
territory: The St. Lawrence valley, the Great Lakes and the Mississippi down to Louisiana
language_faith: French; Catholicism
fact: Fur traders and missionaries spread across half a continent with only about 70,000 settlers. It was lost after Wolfe beat Montcalm on the Plains of Abraham in 1759.

name: Viceroyalty of New Spain
modern_places: Mexico; Guatemala; Honduras; El Salvador; Nicaragua; Costa Rica; Cuba; United States; Philippines
map_places: Mexico; Guatemala; Belize; Honduras; El Salvador; Nicaragua; Costa Rica; Cuba; Dominican Republic; Puerto Rico
territory: Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean islands, the American Southwest and Florida, and the Philippines across the Pacific
language_faith: Spanish and Nahuatl; Catholicism
fact: Its silver mines fed the world economy, and the Manila galleons tied it to China across the Pacific for 250 years.
ruler: Antonio de Mendoza, the first viceroy

name: First Mexican Empire
modern_places: Mexico; Guatemala; Honduras; El Salvador; Nicaragua; Costa Rica; United States
territory: The whole former viceroyalty, from California and Texas down to Costa Rica
language_faith: Spanish; Catholicism
fact: A royalist officer who had switched sides had himself crowned emperor. He lasted ten months, and was shot when he came back from exile.

name: Second Mexican Empire
territory: The central heartland of the country, held by French troops while republicans fought on in the north
language_faith: Spanish; Catholicism
fact: Napoleon III installed a Habsburg archduke as emperor. When the French army left, the republic's forces captured him and shot him at Querétaro.

name: Republic of Texas
territory: The land between the Sabine and the Rio Grande, claiming north as far as today's Wyoming
language_faith: English and Spanish; mostly Protestant settlers
fact: Won independence at San Jacinto weeks after the fall of the Alamo, then spent nine years as a country of its own before joining the United States.

name: Kingdom of Haiti
territory: The northern part of western Hispaniola
language_faith: Creole and French; Catholicism and Vodou
fact: Born from the only slave revolt in history to found a state. Its king built the Citadelle Laferrière, the largest fortress in the Americas, and the palace of Sans-Souci.

name: Federal Republic of Central America
aliases: united provinces of central america; central american federation
modern_places: Guatemala; El Salvador; Honduras; Nicaragua; Costa Rica
territory: Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica
language_faith: Spanish; Catholicism
fact: Formed when the isthmus broke away from Mexico. Wars between liberals and conservatives split it into five countries within two decades.

name: Athenian Empire
territory: The islands and coasts of the Aegean Sea
language_faith: Ancient Greek; the Olympian gods
fact: Its allies' tribute, first kept on a sacred island, paid for the Parthenon. It ended with defeat by Sparta in the Peloponnesian War.

name: Kingdom of Dacia
territory: The Carpathian mountains and the lower Danube
language_faith: An extinct Thracian tongue; worship of Zalmoxis
fact: Its gold drew two Roman invasions. Trajan's Column in Rome shows, scene by scene, the war that ended it in 106.

name: Visigothic Kingdom
territory: Hispania and, at first, southwestern Gaul
language_faith: Latin and Gothic; Arian, then Catholic Christianity
fact: Its people sacked Rome in 410 before settling in the west. Muslim armies crossing from Africa in 711 brought it down within a few years.
ruler: Alaric I, who sacked Rome before the kingdom was founded

name: Ostrogothic Kingdom
territory: Italy, Sicily and the Dalmatian coast
language_faith: Latin and Gothic; Arian Christian rulers over a Catholic people
fact: Its king ruled Italy with Roman officials at his side. Justinian's generals destroyed it in a war that lasted twenty years.

name: Merovingian Kingdom
aliases: merovingians; kingdom of the franks; francia
territory: Gaul and western Germany
language_faith: Latin and Frankish; Catholic Christianity
fact: Its first great king became a Catholic around 496. Later its long-haired kings became figureheads while the mayors of the palace held the real power.

name: Great Moravia
territory: Today's Czechia and Slovakia, with parts of Hungary and Poland
language_faith: Old Slavonic; Christianity, newly arrived
fact: Two missionary brothers from Byzantium came here in 863 and made the first Slavic alphabet. Magyar raiders ended it soon after 900.

name: Caliphate of Córdoba
aliases: caliphate of cordoba; umayyad caliphate of córdoba; al-andalus
territory: Most of the Iberian peninsula and part of North Africa
language_faith: Arabic and Romance; Islam, with large Christian and Jewish communities
fact: Its capital was western Europe's largest and most learned city, with a great mosque of red-and-white arches. It broke into dozens of small taifa kingdoms in 1031.

name: North Sea Empire
territory: England, Denmark, Norway and part of Sweden
language_faith: Old English and Old Norse; Christianity
fact: A Danish king conquered England and ruled three kingdoms at once. Legend says he set his throne on the shore to show his courtiers he could not command the tide.

name: Angevin Empire
territory: England and the western half of France, from Normandy to the Pyrenees
language_faith: French, English and Latin; Catholicism
fact: Built by a count's son and his wife, Eleanor of Aquitaine. Their youngest son lost Normandy, then the battle of Bouvines, and was forced to seal Magna Carta.
capital: None fixed; the court moved between Chinon, Rouen and Westminster

name: Republic of Venice
aliases: venice; venetian republic; serenissima; most serene republic
territory: A lagoon city with the Adriatic coast, Crete, Cyprus and many Greek islands
language_faith: Venetian and Italian; Catholicism
fact: Ruled by an elected doge for a thousand years. Its fleet turned the Fourth Crusade against Constantinople in 1204, and Napoleon ended it in 1797.

name: Republic of Genoa
territory: The Ligurian coast, Corsica, and trading posts around the Black Sea
language_faith: Ligurian and Italian; Catholicism
fact: Its bankers financed the Spanish crown and its colonies ringed the Black Sea. One of its sons sailed west for Spain in 1492.

name: Papal States
aliases: states of the church; pontifical states
territory: Central Italy, from Rome across to Bologna and the Adriatic
language_faith: Italian and Latin; ruled by the head of the Catholic Church
fact: Began with a Frankish king's gift of land in 756. Italian troops took Rome in 1870, and what remains is now the world's smallest country.

name: Crown of Aragon
aliases: aragon; kingdom of aragon; aragonese empire
territory: Northeastern Spain, the Balearics, Sardinia, Sicily and Naples
language_faith: Catalan and Latin, among others; Catholicism
fact: A kingdom joined to the county of Barcelona, it built a Mediterranean empire. A royal marriage in 1469 tied it to Castile.

name: Emirate of Granada
aliases: nasrid kingdom; nasrid emirate; kingdom of granada
territory: The mountains and coast of southern Andalusia, from Gibraltar to Almería
language_faith: Arabic; Islam
fact: The last Muslim state in western Europe, it built the Alhambra. Its surrender in January 1492 completed the Reconquista.

name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
territory: From the Baltic towards the Black Sea: today's Belarus and Ukraine, and part of western Russia
language_faith: Ruthenian and a Baltic tongue; pagan until 1387, then Catholic and Orthodox
fact: Europe's last pagan state became its largest country. It helped crush the Teutonic Knights at Grunwald in 1410, and from 1569 shared a crown with Poland.

name: Teutonic Order State
aliases: state of the teutonic order; teutonic knights; teutonic order; ordensstaat
territory: The southeastern Baltic coast, with Livonia ruled by a sister order
language_faith: German, Latin and Old Prussian; a Catholic crusading order
fact: Crusading knights conquered the pagan Prussians and ruled them from a vast brick castle. Their last grand master turned Lutheran and made the land a duchy in 1525.

name: Kalmar Union
territory: Denmark, Norway and Sweden, with Finland, Iceland and Greenland
language_faith: Danish, Swedish and Norwegian; Catholicism
fact: Three crowns under one monarch. A Danish king's massacre of Swedish nobles in Stockholm in 1520 started the revolt that ended it.
capital: No fixed capital; the kings mostly sat in Copenhagen

name: Second Bulgarian Empire
modern_places: Bulgaria; Romania; Serbia; North Macedonia; Greece
territory: The Balkans between the Danube and the Aegean
language_faith: A South Slavic language; Orthodox Christianity
fact: Two brothers rebelled against Byzantium in 1185. A later tsar captured a Latin emperor of Constantinople, and the Ottomans took its capital in 1393.

name: Serbian Empire
modern_places: Serbia; Kosovo; North Macedonia; Albania; Montenegro; Greece
territory: The western Balkans from the Danube to the Gulf of Corinth
language_faith: South Slavic and Greek; Orthodox Christianity
fact: Its tsar issued a law code still studied today and nearly took Constantinople. The realm broke apart within twenty years of his death.

name: Grand Duchy of Moscow
aliases: muscovy; grand principality of moscow; moscow
territory: The forest lands of northeastern Rus', growing from one town to the Urals
language_faith: East Slavic; Orthodox Christianity
fact: Its princes grew rich collecting tribute for the Mongols. Ivan III tripled its lands, ended that tribute and married the niece of the last Byzantine emperor.

name: Burgundian State
aliases: duchy of burgundy; valois burgundy; burgundian netherlands; burgundy
territory: Two blocks of land: the Low Countries in the north, and a duchy around Dijon in eastern France
language_faith: French and Dutch; Catholicism
fact: Its dukes kept Europe's richest court and paid painters like Van Eyck. The last duke, Charles the Bold, died in battle at Nancy in 1477 and the lands were split.

name: Kingdom of Scotland
territory: The northern third of Great Britain and the Hebrides, later Orkney and Shetland
language_faith: Gaelic, Scots and English; Catholic, then Presbyterian
fact: Won its independence at Bannockburn in 1314. In 1603 its king inherited the English crown, and the two kingdoms merged in 1707.

name: Kingdom of Prussia
territory: Northern Germany from the Rhine to the Niemen, with much of today's Poland
language_faith: German; Lutheran and Reformed Protestantism
fact: Its state was said to be an army with a country attached. Its chancellor, Bismarck, unified Germany around it in 1871.

name: Kingdom of the Two Sicilies
territory: Southern Italy and the large island off its toe
language_faith: Italian and Neapolitan; Catholicism
fact: Italy's first railway ran here in 1839. Garibaldi and his thousand red-shirts overthrew it in 1860, and it was folded into a united Italy.

name: Second French Empire
territory: France, with colonies in Algeria, Senegal, Indochina and the Pacific
language_faith: French; Catholicism
fact: Its emperor, nephew of a more famous one, had Paris rebuilt with grand boulevards. He was captured by the Prussians at Sedan in 1870.

name: Assassination of Julius Caesar
aliases: caesar's assassination; death of caesar; ides of march
territory: The heart of the Mediterranean world
language_faith: About sixty senators, and the dictator they feared would make himself king
fact: Not the old republic they hoped for: civil war followed, and his adopted heir became the first emperor.
capital: A meeting hall in Pompey's theatre complex, Rome

name: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
aliases: fall of rome; end of the western roman empire; deposition of romulus augustulus
territory: The Italian peninsula
language_faith: A Germanic general of the army and a teenage emperor
fact: No new emperor was named in the west. The general ruled Italy as king and sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople.

name: Battle of Tours
aliases: battle of poitiers; battle of tours-poitiers
territory: Western Gaul, between two river cities
language_faith: Frankish infantry against an Umayyad army that had crossed the Pyrenees
fact: The raid was turned back, and the Frankish commander's family rose to become kings. His grandson was Charlemagne.

name: Coronation of Charlemagne
territory: Central Italy
language_faith: A Frankish king and the pope, on Christmas Day
fact: Revived the title of emperor in the west, the seed of the Holy Roman Empire, and angered Constantinople.

name: Battle of Hastings
aliases: norman conquest; hastings; norman conquest of england
territory: The south coast of England
language_faith: A Norman duke's army against an English king's housecarls
fact: The last successful invasion of England. Normans replaced the English nobility, and French words flooded the language.

name: Sealing of Magna Carta
territory: The Thames valley
language_faith: Rebel barons and a king who had lost his lands in France
fact: The pope annulled it within weeks, but it was reissued and became a founding text of the rule of law.
capital: Runnymede, a meadow beside the Thames

name: Black Death reaches Europe
aliases: black death; the plague; bubonic plague; great mortality
modern_places: Italy; France; Spain; United Kingdom; Germany
territory: The ports of the Mediterranean, then the whole continent
language_faith: Genoese galleys from the Black Sea, rats, fleas and everyone else
fact: Killed perhaps a third to a half of the continent. The labour shortage that followed loosened serfdom.
capital: Messina, Sicily, where the first ships landed
ruler: Giovanni Boccaccio, who wrote of it in Florence

name: Fall of Constantinople
aliases: conquest of constantinople; fall of byzantium; siege of constantinople
territory: The strait between Europe and Asia
language_faith: A young Ottoman sultan with giant cannon, against a city of a few thousand defenders
fact: Ended the last remnant of the Roman Empire. The city became the Ottoman capital, and its great church a mosque.
capital: The land walls of the city on the Bosporus

name: Gutenberg's printing press
aliases: printing press; gutenberg bible; movable type; invention of the printing press
territory: The Rhineland
language_faith: A goldsmith, his investors and a workshop of printers
fact: Books became cheap. Within fifty years millions had been printed, and the Reformation would spread on paper.
ruler: Johann Fust, the investor who later sued him

name: Fall of Granada
aliases: end of the reconquista; reconquista; conquest of granada
territory: Southern Iberia
language_faith: The Catholic Monarchs and the last Nasrid emir
fact: Completed the Reconquista. The same year Jews were expelled from Spain, and a Genoese sailor won royal backing.

name: Painting of the Mona Lisa
aliases: mona lisa; la gioconda; da vinci; leonardo da vinci
territory: Tuscany
language_faith: A silk merchant's wife and the painter he hired
fact: It was never delivered: the painter took it to France. Since its theft in 1911 it has been the world's most famous painting.

name: Luther's Ninety-five Theses
aliases: ninety-five theses; 95 theses; reformation; protestant reformation
territory: Saxony, in the Holy Roman Empire
language_faith: A monk and university lecturer, against the sale of indulgences
fact: The Protestant Reformation, which split western Christianity.
capital: Wittenberg, by tradition on the castle church door

name: Defeat of the Spanish Armada
territory: The English Channel and the North Sea
language_faith: About 130 ships of a Catholic king, against English fireships and storms
fact: Most of the fleet was wrecked sailing home around Scotland and Ireland, and England's queen became a legend.

name: Newton's Principia
aliases: principia; principia mathematica; newton's laws; laws of motion; universal gravitation
territory: Eastern England
language_faith: A Cambridge professor, and an astronomer who paid for the printing
fact: Laws of motion and gravity explained the planets and the tides, and stood unchallenged until Einstein.

name: Storming of the Bastille
aliases: bastille day; fall of the bastille; french revolution
territory: Northern France
language_faith: Paris crowds and mutinous soldiers, against a fortress-prison's garrison
fact: Became the symbol of the French Revolution. The monarchy fell three years later.
capital: A fortress-prison on the east side of Paris

name: Battle of Waterloo
territory: The Low Countries
language_faith: A British-led allied army and the Prussians, against a returned emperor
fact: Ended his Hundred Days. He was exiled to St Helena, and Europe was redrawn at Vienna.

name: Assassination of Franz Ferdinand
aliases: sarajevo assassination; franz ferdinand; assassination of archduke franz ferdinand
territory: The Balkans
language_faith: A Bosnian Serb student and the heir to an empire's throne
fact: Within six weeks the great powers were at war: the First World War.

name: Fall of the Berlin Wall
aliases: berlin wall; fall of the wall
territory: Central Europe
language_faith: East German crowds, confused border guards and a party spokesman
fact: Germany reunified within a year, and communist rule across Eastern Europe collapsed.
capital: The checkpoints and the Brandenburg Gate, Berlin

name: Battle of Marathon
territory: Attica
language_faith: Athenian and Plataean hoplites, against a Persian landing force
fact: Saved Athens. A runner's legendary dash with the news gave its name to a race.
capital: The coastal plain northeast of Athens

name: Battle of Thermopylae
territory: Central Greece
language_faith: A few thousand Greeks, led by 300 Spartans, against Xerxes' army
fact: Lost, but the stand became a symbol of sacrifice. The Persian fleet was beaten at Salamis weeks later.

name: Birth of Jesus
aliases: nativity; birth of christ; christmas; jesus
territory: Judea, a client kingdom of Rome
language_faith: A carpenter's family from Galilee, shepherds, and visitors from the east
fact: Christianity, today the world's largest religion, and a calendar counting years from it, slightly miscalculated.
capital: A small town south of Jerusalem
ruler: Herod the Great, king of Judea

name: Enlightenment of the Buddha
territory: The Ganges plain
language_faith: A prince turned wandering ascetic, meditating under a fig tree
fact: Buddhism, which spread across all of Asia.

name: Battle of Gaugamela
territory: Mesopotamia
language_faith: A Macedonian king's army, against the Persian Great King's much larger host
fact: The Persian Empire collapsed. Its king was murdered by his own men the next year.

name: Unification of China
territory: The Yellow River valley
language_faith: The king of the westernmost state, conquering six rivals
fact: One script, one currency, one road gauge, a first emperor, and the name the west still uses for the country.

name: Battle of Red Cliffs
territory: The middle Yangtze
language_faith: Allied southern warlords and their fire ships, against the northern chancellor's fleet
fact: The country stayed split, leading to the Three Kingdoms.

name: The Hijra
territory: The Hejaz, western Arabia
language_faith: The Prophet Muhammad and his followers, leaving Mecca
fact: The first Muslim community. The Islamic calendar counts its years from it.

name: Battle of Talas
territory: Central Asia
language_faith: An Abbasid army and Turkic allies, against a Tang Chinese army
fact: Chinese power in Central Asia ended, and legend says captured papermakers carried their craft west.

name: First Crusade takes Jerusalem
aliases: first crusade; siege of jerusalem; crusades; the crusades
territory: The Levant
language_faith: Frankish knights and pilgrims, against the Fatimid garrison
fact: Founded a Latin kingdom that held the city until Saladin retook it in 1187.
capital: The holy city in the Judean hills

name: Mongol sack of Baghdad
aliases: sack of baghdad; siege of baghdad
territory: Mesopotamia
language_faith: A grandson of Genghis Khan, against the last caliph of a 500-year dynasty
fact: Ended the Abbasid caliphate there. Its libraries' books were said to turn the Tigris black with ink.
capital: The round city on the Tigris

name: Marco Polo's journey
aliases: travels of marco polo; marco polo
territory: Along the Silk Road to the Mongol court
language_faith: A Venetian merchant family and the Great Khan
fact: His book, dictated in a Genoese prison, shaped Europe's picture of Asia. Columbus carried a copy.

name: Voyages of Zheng He
aliases: zheng he; treasure voyages; ming treasure voyages
modern_places: China; Indonesia; Sri Lanka; India; Kenya
territory: From the China Sea across the Indian Ocean
language_faith: A Muslim eunuch admiral and fleets of giant junks
fact: Ming China reached Arabia and East Africa, then stopped sailing and turned inward.
capital: Nanjing, where the fleets were built

name: First Battle of Panipat
territory: The plains north of Delhi
language_faith: A Timurid prince with cannon, against the Delhi sultan's war elephants
fact: Founded the Mughal Empire.

name: Magellan's circumnavigation
territory: Around the whole globe
language_faith: Five Spanish ships and some 270 men, of whom one ship and 18 came home
fact: Proved the world could be sailed around. Its captain was killed on an island on the way.
capital: Mactan, in the Philippines, where the captain fell

name: Battle of Sekigahara
territory: Central Honshu
language_faith: Eastern and western coalitions of lords, about 160,000 men
fact: Its winner became shogun, and his family ruled the country for 250 years.

name: Building of the Taj Mahal
territory: The Yamuna river in northern India
language_faith: A grieving emperor and some 20,000 workers
fact: One of the world's most famous buildings. Its builder was later imprisoned by his son, within sight of it.

name: Battle of Plassey
territory: Bengal
language_faith: East India Company troops, against the Nawab of Bengal, betrayed by his own commander
fact: The Company began to rule Bengal: the start of British India.
capital: A mango grove at Palashi, West Bengal

name: Meiji Restoration
territory: Japan's main island
language_faith: Samurai from southern domains, the last shogun and a teenage emperor
fact: The country industrialised in a generation and became a great power.

name: Eruption of Krakatoa
territory: The Dutch East Indies
language_faith: A volcanic island, and the coastal towns its tsunamis swept away
fact: Heard 4,800 km away. Its ash cooled the world and reddened sunsets for years.
capital: The strait between Java and Sumatra

name: Independence of India
aliases: indian independence; partition of india; partition
territory: South Asia
language_faith: Congress leaders, the Muslim League and the last viceroy
fact: Two new states, and one of the largest migrations in history.

name: Building of the Great Pyramid
aliases: great pyramid; pyramid of giza; pyramids; great pyramid of giza
territory: The Nile valley
language_faith: A Fourth Dynasty king and tens of thousands of paid labourers
fact: The tallest building on Earth for nearly 4,000 years, and the only ancient wonder still standing.

name: Death of Cleopatra
aliases: cleopatra's death; suicide of cleopatra; cleopatra
territory: The Nile delta
language_faith: The last Ptolemaic queen, her Roman lover and Octavian's army
fact: Egypt became Octavian's personal province. Three years later he was Augustus.

name: Battle of Zama
territory: North Africa
language_faith: Rome's army and Numidian cavalry, against a great general's veterans and elephants
fact: Ended the Second Punic War. Carthage gave up its fleet and its empire.

name: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage
aliases: mansa musa's hajj; hajj of mansa musa; mansa musa
territory: Across the Sahara
language_faith: A West African king with thousands of attendants and camels laden with gold
fact: He spent so much gold in Cairo that its value fell for years, and Europe put him on its maps.
capital: Cairo, on the way to Mecca

name: Vasco da Gama reaches India
aliases: vasco da gama; sea route to india
territory: Around Africa to the spice coast
language_faith: Four Portuguese ships and a pilot from the Swahili coast
fact: Opened the sea route from Europe to Asia around Africa, and Portugal built a trading empire.

name: Opening of the Suez Canal
territory: The isthmus between Africa and Asia
language_faith: A French developer, the khedive and many thousands of forced labourers
fact: Cut the sea route from Europe to India by thousands of kilometres.
capital: From Port Said to Suez, via Ismailia

name: Battle of Isandlwana
territory: Southeastern Africa
language_faith: A Zulu army of 20,000, against a British column
fact: Britain's worst defeat by an African army. The kingdom was conquered within months anyway.
capital: Below a sphinx-shaped hill in KwaZulu-Natal

name: Battle of Adwa
territory: The Horn of Africa
language_faith: Ethiopian armies, against an Italian invasion force
fact: Ethiopia kept its independence through the Scramble for Africa.

name: Release of Nelson Mandela
territory: Southern Africa
language_faith: A prisoner of 27 years, and the president who freed him
fact: Apartheid ended, and four years later the prisoner was elected president.
capital: Victor Verster Prison, then Cape Town city hall

name: Columbus reaches the Americas
aliases: columbus; first voyage of columbus; discovery of america; christopher columbus
territory: The Caribbean
language_faith: Three Spanish ships, and the Taíno people
fact: Lasting contact between the Old World and the New, and the exchange of crops, animals and disease.

name: Fall of Tenochtitlan
aliases: conquest of the aztec empire; siege of tenochtitlan; tenochtitlan
territory: The Valley of Mexico
language_faith: Spanish conquistadors and tens of thousands of indigenous allies, against the Mexica
fact: The end of the Aztec Empire. A colonial capital was built on its ruins.
capital: An island city in Lake Texcoco

name: Battle of Cajamarca
territory: The northern Andes
language_faith: 168 Spaniards, against the Inca emperor's escort of thousands
fact: The emperor filled a room with gold as ransom and was executed anyway; the empire fell apart.
capital: A town square in the northern highlands of Peru

name: Landing of the Mayflower
aliases: mayflower; pilgrims; plymouth colony; pilgrim fathers
territory: New England
language_faith: About a hundred English Separatists, and the Wampanoag
fact: A colony whose first harvest feast became the model for Thanksgiving.

name: Declaration of Independence
aliases: american independence; fourth of july; july 4th
territory: The Atlantic seaboard
language_faith: Delegates of thirteen colonies in a Continental Congress
fact: A new country, though the war for it lasted until 1783.

name: Battle of Boyacá
territory: The northern Andes
language_faith: Patriot armies fresh from crossing the Andes, against Spanish royalists
fact: Freed New Granada; Gran Colombia was declared months later.

name: Battle of Gettysburg
territory: The eastern United States
language_faith: Union and Confederate armies, about 160,000 men
fact: The South never invaded the North again. Months later a famous short speech was given on the field.

name: Opening of the Panama Canal
territory: Central America
language_faith: US Army engineers and tens of thousands of Caribbean workers
fact: Ships no longer had to sail around Cape Horn.
capital: Across the isthmus, from Colón to the Pacific

name: Apollo 11 Moon landing
aliases: moon landing; apollo 11; first moon landing
territory: Launched from the Atlantic coast of Florida
language_faith: Three astronauts and some 400,000 engineers and workers
fact: People walked on another world for the first time.
capital: Launched from Cape Kennedy; landed in the Sea of Tranquility

name: Polynesian settlement of New Zealand

territory: The far southwest Pacific
language_faith: Ocean voyagers in double-hulled canoes, from islands far to the northeast
fact: The last large landmass on Earth to be settled. Within two centuries the giant moa birds were extinct.

name: Cook lands at Botany Bay

territory: The east coast of a southern continent
language_faith: A British naval expedition, and the Gweagal people
fact: Britain claimed the east coast, and a convict fleet arrived 18 years later.
capital: Kamay (Botany Bay), south of today's Sydney

name: Mutiny on the Bounty
aliases: bounty mutiny; mutiny on the bounty; hms bounty
